learningObjective: Delineate the responsibilities of an SPMD-style compiler versus a distributed runtime (e.g. NCCL / MPI stack).
stem: Which THREE of the following statements about the division of responsibilities between an SPMD-style compiler (e.g. XLA + GSPMD emitting StableHLO) and a distributed runtime (e.g. NCCL) are correct?

options.text: The compiler decides which collectives (AllReduce, AllGather, All-to-All, ReduceScatter) to insert and at which mesh axes, based on sharding specs; the runtime chooses the internal algorithm (ring, tree, recursive halving) at execution time.
Algorithm selection, message-chunk sizes, and NIC/NVLink lane assignment inside a collective are runtime concerns and are not visible at the SPMD IR level.
Fault tolerance (dead-rank detection, retry, checkpoint restore) is a runtime/framework responsibility; the SPMD compiler does not manage process lifecycle.
Because the compiler needs to reason about performance, it must know each device's NVSwitch domain and PCIe topology at compile time; without this, the emitted IR is topology-incorrect.

explanation: A, B, C reflect the standard division. The compiler operates at the mesh-axis / collective-op level; runtime handles algorithm choice, chunking, NIC selection, and fault tolerance. D is wrong: the IR references mesh axes, not physical devices; topology-aware mapping is a runtime concern (though cost models may consult topology when available).

optionExplanations.A: Correct: compile-time inserts collectives; runtime picks algorithm.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: internal algorithm parameters live at the runtime.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: fault tolerance is a runtime/framework concern.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: physical topology awareness lives at the runtime; compiler references mesh axes.

assumptions: Modern SPMD compiler stack (XLA + GSPMD, StableHLO) and NCCL/MPI-style runtime.
nonImplications: Does not imply the compiler has no cost model; cost models can consult mesh shape.
Does not imply the runtime cannot be topology-aware; NCCL is notably topology-aware.

distractorRationales.D: Wrongly places topology-mapping at compile time.
